name: tutor
system: You are a tutor answering a student's question. Use only the facts provided and cover all of them.

facts: Sunlight is a mix of all colors.
Air molecules scatter short wavelengths like blue much more than long wavelengths like red.
The scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every direction in the sky.
Plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
It takes place in chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll.
Oxygen is released as a by-product.

train.q: What is a derivative in calculus?
facts: A derivative measures the instantaneous rate of change of a function.
It equals the slope of the tangent line at a point.
The derivative of x^2 is 2x.
Earth's axis is tilted by about 23.5 degrees.
The hemisphere tilted toward the Sun gets more direct sunlight and longer days.
Seasons are not caused by Earth's distance from the Sun.

train.q: What is the difference between the mean and the median?
facts: The mean is the sum of the values divided by how many there are.
The median is the middle value when the values are sorted.
The median is less affected by outliers than the mean.

train.q: What is an atom made of?
facts: An atom has a nucleus made of protons and neutrons.
Electrons surround the nucleus.
Protons are positive, electrons are negative, and neutrons have no charge.
The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans.
Most coasts get two high tides a day because water bulges on both the near and far sides of Earth.
The Sun also affects tides, but less than the Moon.

train.q: What is a variable in programming?
facts: A variable is a named place that stores a value.
Its value can change while the program runs.
For example, score = 10 stores the number 10 under the name score.
It applies to right triangles.
It says a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
c is the hypotenuse, the longest side, opposite the right angle.

train.q: Why does ice float on water?
facts: Ice is less dense than liquid water.
When water freezes, its molecules lock into an open hexagonal lattice.
Hydrogen bonds hold the molecules farther apart than in liquid water.

train.q: How do supply and demand set prices?
facts: Prices tend to rise when demand exceeds supply.
Prices tend to fall when supply exceeds demand.
The equilibrium price is where supply and demand match.

train.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
facts: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere.
Climate is the average pattern of weather over decades.
A single cold day says nothing about long-term climate trends.
A prime number is a whole number greater than 1.
Its only divisors are 1 and itself.
2 is the only even prime number.

heldout.q: How does the heart pump blood?
facts: The heart has four chambers.
The right side sends blood to the lungs.
The left side pumps oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body.
Gravity is a force that attracts objects with mass toward each other.
More mass means a stronger pull.
The pull gets weaker as distance increases.

heldout.q: What is the difference between a noun and a verb?
facts: A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea.
A verb expresses an action or a state.
In 'The dog runs', dog is a noun and runs is a verb.
Water evaporates from oceans, lakes, and land.
The vapor condenses into clouds.
It returns to the surface as precipitation such as rain or snow.
A fraction represents part of a whole.
The numerator, on top, says how many parts you have.
The denominator, on the bottom, says how many equal parts make the whole.

heldout.q: Why does the Moon have phases?
facts: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun.
As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different amounts of the lit half.
A full cycle of phases takes about 29.5 days.
DNA is a molecule that carries genetic instructions.
It has a double-helix shape.
Its code is written with four bases: A, T, C, and G.
Inflation is a general rise in prices over time.
It reduces the purchasing power of money.
It is commonly measured with the consumer price index.
An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.
It takes an input and produces an output.
A recipe and a sorting method are both examples.
An ecosystem is a community of living things interacting with each other and their nonliving environment.
Energy flows from the Sun through producers to consumers.
Decomposers recycle nutrients back into the soil.

test.q: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
facts: Speed is how much distance is covered per unit of time.
Velocity is speed together with a direction.
Speed is a scalar and velocity is a vector.
A percentage is a number expressed as a fraction of 100.
50% is the same as one half.
To turn a decimal into a percentage, multiply it by 100.
Earth's crust is broken into tectonic plates.
Stress builds up along faults where plates meet.
When a fault slips suddenly, the energy is released as seismic waves.
A metaphor is a figure of speech that describes one thing as if it were another.
Unlike a simile, it does not use 'like' or 'as'.
'Time is a thief' is a metaphor.

test.q: How do plants take up water?
facts: Roots absorb water from the soil.
Water travels up the plant through tubes called xylem.
Transpiration from the leaves pulls the water upward.

test.q: What is the difference between a virus and a bacterium?
facts: Bacteria are single-celled living organisms.
Viruses are not cells and need a host cell to reproduce.
Antibiotics work against bacteria but not against viruses.
Electric current is the flow of electric charge.
It is measured in amperes.
In metal wires the charge is carried by electrons.
In a democracy, power rests with the citizens.
They use it by voting, either directly or through elected representatives.
Free and fair elections are a core feature.
Gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapor trap heat in the atmosphere.
Without it, Earth would be far colder.
Human emissions are strengthening the effect.
